To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the 3049 strain of polyoma virus produces a transplant antigen in adult hamsters which is capable of inducing immunity against tumor cells produced from the same strain of virus, but which tends to enhance the growth rate of tumor cells induced by lp-D virus; 2) the lp-D strain of polyoma produces a transplant antigen that is capable of inducing resistance to tumor cells induced by itself, but tends to enhance the rate of growth of tumor cells induced from 3049 virus;
The polyoma virus strains 3049 and LP-D induce tumors in hamsters with distinct antigenic characteristics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of transplant immunity to tumor cells induced by polyoma virus.
the role of the host's immune response to the virus in the development of transplant immunity against polyoma virus tumors.
the study of the immune response in the hamster to polyoma virus-induced tumors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3049 and the lp-D viruses produce transplant immunity in hamsters against their own tumors, and that this immunity is not complete and is not transferable to other animals.
the results are not consistent with a simple explanation in terms of the presence of a single transplant antigen.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 2 transplant antigents are different, and that they may be associated with the virus itself, or with the virus-induced tumor cell.
polyoma virus-induced tumors in adult hamsters are heterogeneous in their transplant immunity.
the polyoma virus produces at least 2 types of transplant antigens.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 3049 strain of the polyoma virus is able to produce a transplant immunity in hamsters against its own tumor cells, but not against tumor cells produced in the same host by the lp-D strain of the virus.
there are multiple transplant antigens in vivo, and the presence of these antigens in tumor cells can be used to explain the paradoxical results obtained in our experiments.
the presence of multiple transplant antigens in tumor cells may be a common occurrence and may have profound effects on the immunological behavior of tumor cells in vivo.
